hints.title: Put the opposite side in the cosine rule
hints.body: Let θ=∠PRQ. Its opposite side has length a+2d, and its adjacent sides have lengths a and a+d.
hints.recap: The cosine rule connects an angle to all three sides when the opposite side is identified correctly.
hints.pitfall: The largest side is opposite the angle being asked about.
hints.pause: Write the cosine rule and rearrange to make <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></math> the subject.

recall.reminder: The cosine rule connects an angle to all three sides when the opposite side is identified correctly.

hints.title: Simplify before using the inequality
hints.body: The cosine rule gives cosθ=a2−2ad−3d22a(a+d). Factor the numerator as (a+d)(a−3d).
hints.recap: Factoring can expose the ratio controlled by a given inequality.
hints.pitfall: Cancellation uses <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, a valid positive side length.
hints.pause: Simplify, then apply <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>d</mi><mo>></mo><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> to bound the cosine.

recall.reminder: Factoring can expose the ratio controlled by a given inequality.

hints.title: Use triangle feasibility for the other bound
hints.body: The simplified expression is cosθ=a−3d2a. The sum of the two shorter sides must exceed the longest, giving d<a.
hints.recap: A nondegenerate triangle satisfies strict triangle inequalities, and cosine decreases over angles from 0 to 180 degrees.
hints.pitfall: An upper bound on cosine becomes a lower bound on the angle.
hints.pause: Combine both cosine bounds to find the angle’s open interval.

recall.reminder: A nondegenerate triangle satisfies strict triangle inequalities, and cosine decreases over angles from 0 to 180 degrees.

solution:
The cosine rule gives (a+2d)2=a2+(a+d)2−2a(a+d)cosθ. Rearrangement and factorisation give cosθ=(a+d)(a−3d)2a(a+d)=a−3d2a.

From 3d>2a we get cosθ<−1/2, so θ>120∘. The triangle inequality a+(a+d)>a+2d gives d<a, hence cosθ>−1 and θ<180∘.

Every ratio 2/3<d/a<1 is feasible and yields an angle in this interval. Thus 120∘<θ<180∘: E.
knowledgePattern: Cosine-rule bound combined with triangle feasibility
